items.title: Earl Turbinton Interview, 1990-09-01
items.q: We might have played any like manner or like Ornette-ish or like the great group that Miles had during the late 60s with Tony and Ron and Herbie. And the magic that was happening in those rhythm sections. We were inspired by those things, but also trying to approach it from our own unique, intuitive

ctx.x: Okay. We saw that photography and the other aspects of art could also be brought into that same kind of setting or to bring about a unity, a integration of music and photography, music and painting, the way the mural expressed it. The mural that Eugene Ray designed, for example, was singing all the time or playing all the time. And it was something that was done, but it seemed to fit the mood and the moment or the magic of everything that was happening.

And another amazing aspect of what happened with that is that Eugene had done this drawing on scale size, I mean drawing down a scale, and then he had measurements of how big this was supposed to be on this wall and how big this was supposed to be here and what colors were supposed to happen here. And they were very vivid at that time what we called day glow paints or things that were illuminated more so by black light or the purplish type of ultraviolet light that you see.
